section_summary: This section covers Department of State records from July 1940 to June 1944 relating to Japanese nationality and the citizenship status of Japanese-Americans. It documents efforts by American citizens of Japanese descent, particularly in Hawaii and internment camps, to expatriate from Japan or renounce dual nationality under Japanese nationality laws and the U.S. Nationality Act of 1940. The records also include legal memoranda, congressional inquiries, and public correspondence analyzing birthright citizenship under the Fourteenth Amendment, Japanese legal codes governing military obligation and family registry, and the availability of expatriation statistics.

subfiles.about: Consulate in Kobe requests instructions regarding the citizenship status of dual citizen Tadayoshi Kondo after his father reinstated him in the Japanese family record.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Kobe Despatch 304-305 (July 13, 1940): citizenship of dual national Tadayoshi Kondo, reinstated in the Japanese koseki.
subfiles.title: Citizenship Status of Tadayoshi Kondo

subfiles.about: Department of State informs Radford Mobley that procedures for divesting Japanese nationality fall within the jurisdiction of the Japanese government.
subfiles.from: Department of State (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a November 16, 1940 letter: divestment of Japanese nationality in Hawaii lies with Japan; Far Eastern Affairs will discuss further.
subfiles.title: Procedure for Divestment of Japanese Nationality in Hawaii

subfiles.about: Hawaiian Sugar Planters Association prepares a petition urging the State Department to arrange simplified expatriation procedures with Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a December 10, 1940 Hawaiian Sugar Planters letter asking a simplified expatriation procedure and a petition to State.
subfiles.title: Petition for Simplified Expatriation Procedure in Hawaii

subfiles.about: American Consulate at Nagasaki transmits statistical background data on the application of nationality legislation to registered Americans of Japanese race.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Nagasaki Despatch No. 255 (January 17, 1941): statistics on registered Americans of Japanese race under recent nationality legislation.
subfiles.title: Statistical Data on Registered Americans of Japanese Race in Nagasaki

subfiles.about: Embassy in Tokyo forwards a summary of Japanese press reports on how the new Nationality Act affects Nisei in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 5304 (January 21, 1941): a Japan Times article that Americans of Japanese race failing to return by July 14 lose citizenship under the Nationality Act of 1940.
subfiles.title: Japanese Press Coverage of the Nationality Act of 1940

subfiles.about: Allen Douglas advises on Japanese-American renunciation of Japanese nationality and opposes Hawaiian statehood due to the Japanese majority.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Allen Douglas's January 26, 1941 letter urging easy renunciation of Japanese nationality and opposing Hawaiian statehood.
subfiles.title: Renunciation of Japanese Nationality and Opposition to Hawaiian Statehood

subfiles.about: Delegate Samuel W. King requests permission to present a petition on behalf of Hawaiian citizens of Japanese ancestry regarding expatriation.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Delegate Samuel King's January 27, 1941 request to present an expatriation petition for Hawaii's Japanese-ancestry citizens.
subfiles.title: Request by Delegate Samuel W. King to Present Expatriation Petition

subfiles.about: Consulate at Osaka reports that William Merrell Vories renounced American citizenship after being adopted into his Japanese wife's family.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Osaka Despatch No. 166: William Merrell Vories renounced American citizenship, having acquired Japanese nationality by adoption as Hitotsuyanagi.
subfiles.title: Renunciation of American Citizenship by William Merrell Vories

subfiles.about: American Loyalty League of Fresno inquires how to demonstrate Nisei loyalty and urges legislation ending dual nationality.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to the American Loyalty League's March 31, 1941 letter asking how to publicize Japanese-American loyalty and urging legislation ending dual citizenship.
subfiles.title: Inquiry by American Loyalty League on Allegiance and Dual Citizenship

subfiles.about: Consulate at Osaka transmits a letter from Naoki Nishiyama expressing loyalty to Japan as typical of Japan-educated Nisei.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Osaka Despatch No. 44: Naoki Nishiyama's letter professing loyalty to Japan, typical of Kibei.
subfiles.title: Letter of Naoki Nishiyama Regarding Loyalty of Japan-Educated Nisei

subfiles.about: Embassy in Tokyo reports inquiries by Japanese-Americans in Japan regarding expatriation under Section 402 of the Nationality Act of 1940.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 137 (January 20, 1941): about 4,000 Japanese-Americans in Japan ask whether they will be expatriated after six months under Section 402.
subfiles.title: Status of Japanese-Americans in Japan under Section 402 of Nationality Act

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum analyzes conflicting estimates of dual citizens in Hawaii seeking expatriation from Japan.
subfiles.from: Department of State (Division of Far Eastern Affairs - Herbert P. Fales)
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Fales's April 10, 1941 memorandum on estimates of Hawaii dual citizens seeking expatriation: 1,600 versus 3,500, and 1,700 applicants in 1940.
subfiles.title: Estimates of Japanese Dual Citizens in Hawaii Seeking Expatriation

subfiles.about: Department of the Interior forwards a petition signed by over 30,000 Hawaiian citizens of Japanese ancestry requesting simplified expatriation.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to an April 29, 1941 Interior letter forwarding a petition signed by over 30,000 Hawaii Japanese-Americans seeking simplified expatriation.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Hawaii Expatriation Petition by Department of the Interior

subfiles.about: Senate of Hawaii transmits Senate Concurrent Resolution No. 35 requesting State Department assistance to simplify Japanese expatriation.
subfiles.from: Senate of the Territory of Hawaii
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Hawaii Senate Concurrent Resolution No. 35 (April 24, 1941) asking State to secure simplified expatriation procedures.
subfiles.title: Hawaii Senate Concurrent Resolution No. 35 on Expatriation Procedure

subfiles.about: Japanese American Citizens League of San Diego forwards resolutions pledging allegiance to the United States and renouncing Japanese rights.
subfiles.from: Japanese American Citizens League of San Diego (Otsuka)
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to San Diego JACL resolutions of January 24, 1942 pledging allegiance to the US and repudiating Japanese Empire rights.
subfiles.title: Resolutions of the Japanese American Citizens League of San Diego

subfiles.about: U.S. censorship officers intercept and condemn two expatriation applications from Hawaiian residents addressed to the Japanese Consulate General.
subfiles.summary: Censorship record of a December 1941 letter from Shigeko Asato in Hawaii to the Japanese Consulate General enclosing two expatriation applications, a certificate and koseki.
subfiles.title: Censorship Record NY 5309-42: Expatriation Applications of Shigeko Asato

subfiles.about: Representative Francis Case inquires into the dual citizenship and expatriation status of Lillian Higashi through the Chicago Consulate.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to an April 2, 1942 letter on Lillian Higashi's dual citizenship and whether her expatriation was completed before the war.
subfiles.title: Expatriation Status of Lillian Higashi

subfiles.about: Flournoy discusses Senator Stewart's proposed legislation to strip Japanese-Americans of citizenship and potential reversal of Wong Kim Ark.
subfiles.from: Department of State Legal Adviser (Richard W. Flournoy)
keywords: United States v. Wong Kim Ark
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a February 11, 1942 memo on Senator Stewart's proposal to deprive American-born Japanese of citizenship and reverse Wong Kim Ark.
subfiles.title: Senator Stewart's Proposal on Expatriating American-Born Japanese

subfiles.about: Embassy in Tokyo forwards a magazine article by Professor Takizo Matsumoto analyzing the second-generation Japanese problem.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Grew's April 6, 1942 despatch with Prof. Takizo Matsumoto's article on second-generation Japanese.
subfiles.title: Magazine Article by Professor Takizo Matsumoto on Second-Generation Japanese

subfiles.about: War Relocation Authority submits evacuee statements expressing dual citizenship and seeking renunciation of American citizenship.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to War Relocation Authority submissions of evacuee statements claiming dual citizenship and wishing to renounce American citizenship.
subfiles.title: War Relocation Authority Submissions on Evacuee Renunciation Statements

subfiles.about: State Department issues instructions to the Legation in Bern regarding acquisition of Japanese nationality by Frank Quini and siblings.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to an August 24, 1943 instruction to Bern on Frank Quini's citizenship and his siblings' acquisition of Japanese nationality.
subfiles.title: Instruction to Bern Regarding Citizenship of Frank Quini

subfiles.about: Legation in Bern transmits affidavit and baptismal certificate seeking repatriation exchange inclusion for Emilia Quini.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Bern Despatch No. 5970: Emilia Quini's affidavit and baptismal certificate, asking reexamination so she can join a diplomatic exchange.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Bern Regarding Repatriation Exchange of Emilia Quini

subfiles.about: State Department informs Spanish Embassy that U.S. citizens interned at Gila River cannot legally renounce U.S. citizenship while in the country.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a March 8, 1943 memorandum to the Spanish Embassy: no statutory procedure lets American citizens in the US renounce citizenship, as with Gila River internees.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Inability of Gila River Internees to Renounce Citizenship

subfiles.about: Flournoy advises Passport Division that dual national children lose Japanese nationality unless registered at a consulate within two weeks of birth.
subfiles.from: Department of State Legal Adviser (Richard W. Flournoy)
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Flournoy's March 26, 1943 memo: under Article 20(2), US-born children lose Japanese nationality unless registered at a Japanese consulate within two weeks.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Consular Registration under Article 20(2) of Japanese Law

subfiles.about: Vincent Cope argues that American-born Japanese are not U.S. citizens because dual nationality excludes them from U.S. jurisdiction.
subfiles.summary: Vincent Cope argues the Fourteenth Amendment does not confer citizenship on American-born Japanese, citing dual allegiance under Japanese nationality law, Elk v. Wilkins and Gonzales v. Williams.
subfiles.title: Letter from Vincent Cope Challenging Citizenship of American-Born Japanese

subfiles.about: Office of Coordination and Review suggests that Legal Adviser Hackworth sign the reply to Vincent Cope.
subfiles.from: Department of State (Office of Coordination and Review - C. R. Rockwell)
subfiles.summary: Rockwell recommends that the reply to Vincent Cope be drafted for Legal Adviser Hackworth's signature, with changes marked on the blue draft.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip Regarding Draft Reply to Vincent Cope
subfiles.to: Department of State Legal Adviser (Green H. Hackworth)

subfiles.about: Flournoy analyzes Vincent Cope's letter, noting contrasting loyalty between Nisei soldiers and Japan-educated Kibei.
subfiles.from: Department of State Legal Adviser (Richard W. Flournoy)
subfiles.summary: Flournoy tells Hackworth, Salisbury and Ballantine that Cope understands dual nationality problems; Nisei soldiers are loyal while Kibei mostly favor Japan, so extended debate is undesirable.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Vincent Cope Letter and Loyalty of Dual Nationals
subfiles.to: Green H. Hackworth, Laurence Salisbury, and Joseph W. Ballantine

subfiles.about: State Department provides Vincent Cope with legal citations on the citizenship status of children born to alien parents.
subfiles.from: Department of State Legal Adviser (Green H. Hackworth)
keywords: United States v. Wong Kim Ark
subfiles.summary: Hackworth refers Cope to authorities on birthright citizenship, including Wong Kim Ark, Van Dyne and Moore's Digest. Includes the final letter and the marked draft.
subfiles.title: Letter to Vincent Cope Citing Authorities on Birthright Citizenship

subfiles.about: Flournoy advises Hackworth that Japanese law does not permit persons of Japanese descent to acquire Japanese nationality while in the U.S.
subfiles.from: Department of State Legal Adviser (Richard W. Flournoy)
subfiles.summary: Flournoy tells Hackworth that US-born persons of Japanese descent generally cannot acquire Japanese nationality while in the US, answering Rep. Gearhart's inquiry and noting passport renewals and Tule Lake repatriation cases.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Acquisition of Japanese Nationality While in the United States

subfiles.about: State Department discusses policy regarding the departure and exchange of individuals possessing dual U.S. and Japanese nationality.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to an April 30, 1943 communication to the Spanish Embassy on US policy toward exchanging dual US-Japanese nationals (311.9416/560).
subfiles.title: U.S. Policy Regarding Exchange of Dual U.S.-Japanese Nationals

subfiles.about: State Department transmits a five-page memorandum quoting Japanese nationality laws and ordinances to Representative Bertrand W. Gearhart.
subfiles.from: Department of State Legal Adviser (Green H. Hackworth)
subfiles.summary: Letter dated November 23, 1943 from Legal Adviser Green H. Hackworth to Representative Bertrand W. Gearhart, transmitting a comprehensive five-page memorandum on Japanese nationality legislation. The memorandum provides English translations of Articles 1, 7, 11, 20(2), 24, and 25-27 of Law No. 66 of 1899 as revised in 1916 and 1924, outlining rules governing jus sanguinis paternity, naturalization domicile conditions, retroactive forfeiture of Japanese nationality for children born in designated foreign countries (including the U.S.), and military service exceptions under Article 24 preventing males 17 and older from losing nationality without completing active duty. It also incorporates Imperial Ordinance No. 26 of November 17, 1924 detailing procedural regulations for birth reports, renunciation through Japanese diplomatic missions, and recovery of nationality. The subfile includes the transmittal letter, the original memorandum, and three identical carbon copies preserved in State Department records.
subfiles.title: Letter and Memorandum for Representative Bertrand W. Gearhart on Japanese Nationality Laws

subfiles.about: Vincent Cope argues that Selective Service 4-C draft status and Japanese religious beliefs demonstrate that Nisei are foreign subjects.
subfiles.summary: Cope argues Selective Service Class 4-C status proves alien status, Japan's nationality law makes dual nationals Japanese subjects, and ancestor worship may conflict with loyalty to the US.
subfiles.title: Letter from Vincent Cope on Selective Service Status and Japanese Nationality Laws

subfiles.about: State Department declines to express an official legal opinion on Vincent Cope's theoretical citizenship arguments.
subfiles.from: Department of State Legal Adviser (Green H. Hackworth)
subfiles.summary: Hackworth tells Cope the Department cannot express an official opinion without a specific case, though his views are noted.
subfiles.title: Letter to Vincent Cope Declining to Render Legal Opinion

subfiles.about: Vincent Cope forwards to Secretary Cordell Hull a copy of his letter to Attorney General Biddle arguing that Nisei are enemy aliens.
subfiles.summary: Cope sends Hull his June 15, 1944 letter to Attorney General Biddle arguing American-born Japanese are exclusively Japanese subjects and enemy aliens unless naturalized by Congress.
subfiles.title: Letter from Vincent Cope to Cordell Hull Transmitting Letter to Attorney General Biddle

subfiles.about: State Department transmits a memorandum to Representative Clarence E. Hancock regarding acquisition of Chinese or Japanese nationality.
subfiles.summary: State sends Rep. Hancock a memorandum by Swanson on American citizens acquiring Chinese or Japanese nationality, apologizing for the delay.
subfiles.title: Letter to Representative Clarence E. Hancock on Acquiring Chinese or Japanese Nationality

subfiles.about: L. Curtis Guise requests official statistics on American-born Japanese who expatriated under Japanese nationality laws.
subfiles.summary: L. Curtis Guise asks Grew for statistics on American-born Japanese who expatriated under Japan's 1916 and 1924 nationality laws.
subfiles.title: Inquiry by L. Curtis Guise Regarding Expatriation Statistics

subfiles.about: Joseph C. Grew informs L. Curtis Guise that the State Department has no statistics on Japanese expatriation by Nisei.
subfiles.from: Department of State (Office of Far Eastern Affairs - Joseph C. Grew)
subfiles.summary: Grew replies State has no statistics on expatriations, since they were not reported to US authorities; records exist only in Japanese archives.
subfiles.title: Letter from Joseph C. Grew to L. Curtis Guise on Absence of Expatriation Records
